annotations.text:
PARCEL Fund — fractional Bali villa marketplace
Muted turquoise #6CC1C6 used sparingly: primary buttons, active tabs, selected nav, progress fills, status dots. Everything else is a neutral grey ramp on near-black. Glass panels, soft shadows.

Property artwork is generated, not photographed: a seeded generator draws each villa's elevation — open pavilions under steep alang-alang roofs, timber posts, lit interiors, pool and palms — so every listing gets its own building. Change a listing's seed or type (villa / resort / estate / land) and it redraws.

Explore opens on a stats header: platform figures grouped as one bracketed instrument cluster on the left (investment amount large, dividends and investors stacked beside it), and on the right the viewer's own position (villas owned, dividends earned, claimable now) above a Live buys panel: three rows at a time, each new purchase pushing the stack up from the bottom. The investment amount and investor count step on the same 26s cadence, so the figures move as the feed moves. Then 24H Trending (an auto-running carousel, hover to pause), a Movers leaderboard ranked by 24h price change (ranked by purchases over the last 24h), then Filled soon (closest to fully funded), then Early bird sale — the featured listing with quick buy — closing on a Why us banner. Marketplace is the full catalogue — 23 listings across real Bali micro-locations (Batu Bolong, Berawa, Pererenan, Bingin, Balangan, Sayan, Penestanan, Sidemen, Amed, Munduk, Nusa Lembongan and more), grouped under five sponsors. Type filters, a card grid that opens on the first 12, and a status table. The sidebar switches between them; a live purchase feed runs under the top bar on both (hover pauses it).

Locations are real Bali areas; villa, sponsor and wallet names are invented, and every price, yield, occupancy and funding figure is sample data for feeling out the flow. Nothing here maps to a property that exists or an offering anyone can buy. The PT PMA / leasehold structure shown on the deed page is a placeholder too — Indonesian foreign-ownership structuring is a question for local counsel, not a design decision.
